# Tendkit

> Customer support you own: a shared inbox, tickets and a customer portal that you copy into your own app with the shadcn CLI. Customer emails, WhatsApp and SMS become tickets your team answers next to the customer's account. MIT licensed.

Tendkit targets Next.js (App Router), Tailwind 4, shadcn/ui, TanStack Query and Drizzle (Postgres, or SQLite/Cloudflare D1). Channel adapters use only fetch and WebCrypto, so they run on Cloudflare Workers, Node, Bun and Deno.

## Install

`npx shadcn@latest add https://tendkit.softwaresavants.dev/r/support.json https://tendkit.softwaresavants.dev/r/support-postgres.json https://tendkit.softwaresavants.dev/r/support-ui.json https://tendkit.softwaresavants.dev/r/channel-resend.json`

Registry items: support (core), support-postgres, support-d1, support-ai (optional AI engine), support-ai-postgres, support-ai-d1, support-ui, channel-resend, channel-microsoft365, channel-gmail, channel-smtp, channel-twilio, channel-whatsapp, channel-telegram, channel-api. Each is at https://tendkit.softwaresavants.dev/r/<item>.json.

## How to integrate (for coding agents)

1. Install the items above with the shadcn CLI (server items into the API package, support-ui into the web app in a monorepo).
2. Export the support schema from the Drizzle schema and generate a migration. Don't apply migrations without asking.
3. Create the service with createSupport({ store, storage, channels, directory, notify, acknowledgement, fromName, portalChannelId, ignoreFrom, team, teamEmail, replyAll }).
4. Implement the SupportDirectory: identify (sender to user and customer/account), searchCustomers, getCustomers, listAgents. This is the only product-specific part.
5. Route POST /api/webhooks/support/[channel] to support().handleWebhook(channel, request). Call support().runScheduled() from a cron every few minutes.
6. Expose the agent methods (listTickets, getTicket, reply, addNote, assign, setStatus, linkCustomer, changeContact, uploadAttachment, attachmentUrl, counts, listAgents, searchCustomers) and support().portal through the app's own API behind its own auth; implement SupportClient with them and render SupportInbox/SupportTicket inside SupportProvider.
7. Optional AI (triage, one-line summaries, suggested replies; agents always review and send): add support-ai-postgres or support-ai-d1, export the ai-schema and migrate, then pass ai: supportAi({ model, store: createPostgresAiStore(db), knowledge: [docsFromUrl("https://…/llms-full.txt")], defer }) to createSupport. model is any Vercel AI SDK LanguageModel; Tendkit imports only the "ai" package. Add describeCustomer(customerId) to the directory for account facts. Expose support().ai (refine, writeUp, translate, draft, discardSuggestion, setInsight, getSettings, updateSettings, syncKnowledge, listKnowledgeSources) and put the same methods under ai on the SupportClient; map the inbox's sort: "priority" to listTickets. Customer messages go to the configured model provider. Voice in the reply box (one microphone button; an empty box takes spoken notes through writeUp, a box with text takes a spoken change through refine, or "Insert as spoken" for plain dictation; Escape cancels, Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+Space toggles, two-minute limit): pass transcriptionModel (any AI SDK TranscriptionModel) and optionally transcriptionOptions: ({ language }) => providerOptions to supportAi, expose support().ai.transcribe({ audio, language? }) => { text, language } (audio is a Blob, Uint8Array or ArrayBuffer up to 10 MB, never stored) and add the optional transcribe({ audio: Blob }) to client.ai. Without client.ai.transcribe the screens use the browser's Web Speech API in the SupportProvider locale; with neither the button is hidden. A transcription model is more accurate for languages such as Arabic and French. When the browser listens, it uses SupportProvider's speechLocale (default: locale); pass a region such as "fr-FR" when the UI locale is bare "fr". Memory (needs the 0002_memory migration; every client method is optional and the screens hide what's missing): approved answers are the drafts' most trusted source, cited as { type: "answer" }, and agents insert one by typing "/" at the start of a line in the reply box, with {name}, {company} and {agent} filled in and no model call. Expose support().ai.listApprovedAnswers(), generaliseAnswer({ ticketId, text }) => { title, text, language } (takes the customer's details out of a reply for review), saveApprovedAnswer({ id?, title, text, language?, ticketId?, gapId?, actorId }), deleteApprovedAnswer(id), listGuidanceSuggestions(), decideGuidanceSuggestion({ id, accept, rule?, actorId }), listGaps(), dismissGap({ id, actorId }) and draftArticle({ gapId } | { ticketIds }) => { title, markdown }, and add the same names to client.ai (the client passes { id } objects; the server adds actorId). Drafts an agent edits before sending are kept: the same customer's earlier replies go into that customer's later drafts as they were sent; other customers only ever get a one-sentence style note that is dropped if it holds a digit, link, name from the ticket or five words in a row from the conversation (shareStyleNotes: false keeps every correction within its customer). runScheduled draws those notes on each run and, once a day, proposes guidance rules from heavily edited drafts (never applied until a person accepts) and files unanswered questions (cannot_answer suggestions and discarded drafts) under gaps. supportAi also takes an optional embedder: { embed(texts) => number[][] } to order found corrections by meaning.
8. For email: use a receiving subdomain (e.g. in.acme.com) for the reply address, keep the main mailbox where it is, and copy mail to the receiving address. The Resend adapter needs a Full access API key to read received mail.

- [Webhooks and scheduling](https://tendkit.softwaresavants.dev/docs/webhooks): the route, responses, runScheduled

- [Customer portal](https://tendkit.softwaresavants.dev/docs/portal)
- [Theming](https://tendkit.softwaresavants.dev/docs/theming)
- [AI](https://tendkit.softwaresavants.dev/docs/ai): supportAi options, providers, knowledge sources, account facts, deferral, client.ai, voice, memory (approved answers, learning from edits, guidance suggestions, gaps, articles), privacy
- [Email setup](https://tendkit.softwaresavants.dev/docs/email): receiving domains, threading, trimming, automatic mail, authentication
- [Channels](https://tendkit.softwaresavants.dev/docs/channels): resend, microsoft365, gmail, smtp, twilio, whatsapp, telegram, api, and writing your own (/docs/channels/<name>)
- [Upgrading](https://tendkit.softwaresavants.dev/docs/upgrading)
- [Live demo](https://tendkit.softwaresavants.dev/demo)
